name: Name
title: Waking the Dead: Part 4
body: By Aeryn Rudel

name: Name
title: Waking the Dead: \nWhat Has Gone Before

name: Name
body: In Waking the Dead: "Part One—Ghost of a Chance," the warcaster Aiakos delivers Wraithbinder Nekane to the shores of western Immoren to scout places of power that might serve Dominarch Deneghra’s plans. Nekane first investigates the power of an ancient ruin, Nine Stone, to see if its power might serve to build the Well of Annihilation, an ancient Cryxian design believed to be powerful enough to pull a god from Urcaen. But Nine Stone proves to be far too powerful to control, so Nekane and her forces move on to meet with the Orgoth warlord Sabbreth, who suffers under the possession of the artifact the Lash of Horva, and bring these allies up to date regarding Deneghra’s plan. Sabbreth has doubts that Nine Stone is too powerful to control, but she concedes that Nekane, under Deneghra’s command, must know better and offers Orgoth reinforcements to provide support as Nekane continues her scouting mission for other places of power. But recalling Deneghra’s warning that the Orgoth are not long-term allies and are likely to seek domination over Cryx, Nekane rejects Sabbreth’s offer and departs to continue her mission.

name: Name
body: In Waking the Dead: "Part Two—Spirits of the Deep," Swift Sergeant Dana Thorne of Cygnar arrives at Nine Stone in search of evidence of a Cryxian incursion while farther inland, the ones they seek, led by Wraithbinder Nekane, approach their next destination: Dagger Deep, ruins located in an abandoned Rhulic mine…that turns out not to be abandoned after all. Nekane and her forces decimate the Rhulfolk who try to defend the mine before descending into its depths. There, they find evidence that the Rhulfolk had previously battled and lost to cephalyx, a race of subterranean humanoids that used bioengineered to alter themselves into underground horrors. When Nekane and her forces reach the dark ruins of Dagger Deep in a massive cavern far below, the remnants of the cephalyx hive await them on the edge of a vast charnel pit, filled with the corpses the cephalyx have acquired over time. Yet they are no match for the Cryxians, who destroy them, though at a great cost to their own forces. Nekane is not concerned, however—she recognizes that so many corpses in one place, though not good enough to serve as a place to construct their Well of Annihilation or even a necrofactorium, will give her and her master necrotech the resources they need to build a horrifying Cryxian concept: a colossal called a hellraker.

name: Name
body:
In Waking the Dead: "Part Three—Raising the Specter of Ruin," after following Nekane’s trail to Dagger Deep, Swift Sergeant Dana Thorne of Cygnar, recognizing that her forces would be slaughtered if they followed the Cryxians into the mine, diverts to Fort Whiterock, the only sizeable military presences in the upper Wyrmwalls. There, she meets with Duke Sunbright, who not only grants her additional forces but tells her of a second entrance to the mines in a canyon with only one way in or out…
In the weeks of underground work since taking the mine, Nekane’s master necrotech, Chatterbane, has delivered to her two powerful bonejacks, Raptors, but he has insufficient metal and machinery to finish the hellraker colossal. Certain the mountains have other inhabitants, Nekane takes a small force and begins to search the mines and its caverns and tunnels, leaving Chatterbane to continue his work. Days later, when she discovers a previously unknown opening out into the sunlight in a canyon, Nekane is sure she will now find the resources she needs—but exiting the mine, she walks directly into an ambush by Duke Sunbright’s soldiers. Fleeing, she winds her way deeper into the canyon, only to encounter Duke Sunbright and more soldiers, along with an Ironclad warjack. Despite causing massive damage to the enemy, Nekane loses all of her forces and barely escapes with her life into the tree line and temporary safety. There, she collapses.

name: Name
body:
When she awakens, it’s night, and as she tries to determine which way to go to return to the mine, she feels the distant presence of pain, murder, and death. Following it for hours, she emerges into a clearing of scorched earth, a place she knows as the site of the Vicarate Slaughter, where the Orgoth had massacred hundreds of Morrowan priests. It’s here, she realizes, that she could form the Well of Annihilation.
But there in the moonlight, she discovers she is not alone.
She meets Discerptor Eviscerus, a rotted immortal monstrosity who had served Cryx for hundreds of years, scavenging on the mainland for new technology and ancient secrets. Nekane recognizes a potential ally, and she convinces Eviscerus to help her find the resources her master necrotech will require to complete the hellraker colossal. And though clearly insane, Eviscerus provides her more aid than she could have imagined—he leads her to a secret cache with dozens of mechanithralls, bonjacks, even helljacks. Most significantly, this is but one of dozens of stockpiles Eviscerus has hidden in the mountains.

name: Name
body: And Nekane intends to make use of them all.

name: Name
body: Swift Sergeant Dana Thorne stared at the blank scrap of parchment spread out on the back of her breastplate, which she was using a makeshift field desk. She held a quill pen in her hand, the nib black with ink, but no words came. She had no family of her own—the endless wars in the Iron Kingdoms had left her both childless and a widow—so she rarely put pen to paper for anything but official reports. But Gendry had had a family, and as his commanding officer and his friend, it was her job to write to tell them what had happened to their husband and father. She closed her eyes and grimaced. How could you even describe such a thing? It wasn’t just death—that would be easy enough to explain, if painful. Gendry hadn’t fallen from a bullet wound or a sword blow. He hadn’t just died at all. He’d been . . . extinguished. Why had he been so brave? Why had he been so damned stupid? He’d attacked the Cryxian warcaster—Wraithbinder Nekane, she’d called herself—with his knife and inflicted a trivial wound when he could have just stayed back, stayed safe.

name: Name
body:
The image of Gendry’s corpse rose to the surface of Dana’s mind. She was no stranger to blood and death, but the look on her old friend’s face, the rictus of absolute horror and despair, would haunt her for the rest of her days. How could she communicate to his family that his very essence, the core of his being, had been ripped out and devoured? It was too monstrous for something so mundane as ink and paper.
"Sergeant Thorne?" a voice said, drawing Dana’s gaze up. One of the Sunbright Yeoman stood over her—young, fair-haired, clad in the white leather armor of the duke’s rangers.
"What is it, Killian?" Dana said, grateful for any excuse to set her pen down.
"There’s been an . . . incident with the Cryxian machines."
That got Dana’s attention. Wisely, Duke Sunbright had set a guard over the wreckage of the bonejack and the helljack they’d destroyed, thinking Nekane might attempt to salvage them. "Did the guards see something?"
Killian paled and shook his head. "It’s easier if I show you."
***

name: Name
body:
They’d dragged the wreckage of the Cryxian machines a fair distance from their camp. The shattered necromechanika stank of necrotite and Morrow knew what else. The three rangers who drew the short straws and guard duty had had to wear cloth soaked in wine over their mouths to keep from gagging. But the stink was the least of their worries now.
The guards had been dismembered with a bladed weapon, but it was no crude butchery. Limbs and heads had been removed with surgical precision, flesh and bone parted with expert skill.
Without a word, Dana squatted down to examine the nearest corpse. The top of the ranger’s head had been neatly sheared away, exposing gleaming white bone and glistening brain matter. The ranger’s rifle was slung, his knife still in the sheath. Death had taken him before he could even reach for his weapons. "No one heard anything?"
"Nothing, Sergeant," Killian replied. "Their relief found them like this."
Dana got up and walked over to where two more corpses lay next to the wreckage of the bonejack. The helljack, however, was gone. The only sign it had been there was a great, black stain—some unguessable necromechanikal fluid—soiling the ground.

name: Name
body:
"Does Duke Sunbright know?" Dana asked. The duke had withdrawn to Fort Whiterock shortly after the battle with the Cryxian warcaster, taking half his Sunbright Yeoman to resupply and send word of their discovery to the garrisons in Fharin and Ironhead Station. He’d left Dana in charge of the other half to patrol the area and look for signs of their quarry.
Killian shook his head. "No, Sergeant. I thought it best to tell you first."
"All right. Send a runner to Whiterock now."
"With what message?"
Gendry’s corpse again bloomed in Dana’s mind, but she replaced this vision with another, more welcome image. She saw the Cryxian warcaster, dead-pale skin splashed with crimson, the hilt of Dana’s knife jutting from her skull. It brought a grim smile to the swift sergeant’s lips. "Tell him she’s close, and all we have to do is wait."

name: Name
body:
Nekane stood before an old helljack of a type with which she was unfamiliar. The machine had been relegated to the darkest corner of one of Eviscerus’ many caches, seemingly dismissed, moldering away in the dark, not much different than the warcaster himself.
The helljack resembled a Slayer, though its furnace was bulkier, and instead of deathclaws, it was armed with a pair of scythe-liked blades. Patches of rust pocked its hull like cancerous growths, a state not unusual for the machines she’d found in Eviscerus’ stockpiles. The strange warcaster had squirreled away dozens of helljacks and bonejacks and then, over the centuries, simply forgotten about them, leaving them to slowly degrade into useless scrap. In fact, her initial elation at discovering Eviscerus’ hidden army had deflated significantly over the last few weeks as she examined cache after cache and found only a handful of the machines that could be restored to working order.
"The Eviscerator helljack was designed by Discerptor Eviscerus in 499 AR," Eviscerus said from behind Nekane in his odd encyclopedic tone. "Lich Lord Asphyxious preferred other designs, simpler to mass produce, such as the Slayer."

name: Name
body:
"Does this Eviscerator function?" Nekane said without turning around.
Silence, and then one of the few direct answers Eviscerus had given to the hundreds of questions Nekane had asked of him: "No."
"I thought not," Nekane said with a sigh. She left the moldering helljack behind and walked between more inert ’jacks and dust-covered thralls. Eviscerus scuttled after her. This was the tenth and last of the caches she’d examined, and the final tally, out of dozens of helljacks and bonejacks and hundreds of thralls, was strikingly anemic. Directing Chatterbane’s work, she’d managed to restore two Slayers, a pair of Deathrippers, and roughly forty mechanithralls. Not exactly the overwhelming force she’d hoped for, and even with the Furies and Eviscerus added to the mix, she felt less than confident she could defeat the Cygnaran forces that had nearly destroyed her a just few short weeks ago.
There were still too many variables. For one, the Cygnarans outnumbered her, and if they acquired reinforcements from either Fharin or Ironhead Station, her chances of destroying them and securing the site of the Vicarate Slaughter dwindled to nothing. In addition, though Eviscerus was a powerful and experienced warcaster, his mental state was far from stable. He drifted in and out of lucidity, and after he’d flown into a near-panic at the mention of the Orgoth, she could hardly confide in him about her ultimate goals. Still, she could not reliably control so many warjacks on her own, and she’d need Eviscerus in the battle to come.

name: Name
body:
Nekane splashed her way through puddles of dank water—this cache lay beneath a shallow forest pond, and the ceiling leaked steadily into the darkened space—until she reached the opening to a narrow, subterranean passage. Eviscerus had linked all his caches via a network of tunnels that spiderwebbed beneath the Wyrmwalls. One of these meandering passageways eventually connected to the cephalyx hive where Chatterbane was still working away on what Nekane hoped would be the crowning piece in her burgeoning army.
***
When she emerged from the tunnel that connected Eviscerus’ cache to the cephalyx hive, Nekane saw that Chatterbane had, indeed, been his usual industrious self. The great vault that had once only contained the abattoir where the cephalyx had disposed of unneeded organic components was now aswarm with activity. Dozens of mechanithralls moved, ant-like, through the vast cavern, ferrying raw materials or pieces of finished machinery from place to place.
At the center of all this activity was the dire shape of the hellraker. It was still mostly skeletal, though a blackened iron carapace had begun to take shape on the great helljack’s upper half. Still, it appeared weeks away from completion, and Nekane grimaced in disappointment as she walked through the small necrofactorium looking for Chatterbane. Eviscerus followed, muttering softly to himself. Most of his words were inane babble she could hardly identify, but he occasionally made a comment about a bonejack or a thrall that almost sounded sane.

name: Name
body: Nekane found Chatterbane in the new helljack bay, hunkered over a worktable, diagrams and schematics spread out before him. When he saw her and Eviscerus approaching, he scuttled forward, his appendages waving in agitation. "Wraithbinder Nekane," Chatterbane said, "the state of these helljacks and thralls is unacceptable. The time and resources needed to bring them back to something even resembling operating parameters is, well, to put it bluntly, appalling." The necrotech turned to Eviscerus. "How you could let your machines fall into this level of disrepair is—" "Chatterbane," Nekane said sharply, cutting off the necrotech, "Discerptor Eviscerus has supplied us with resources and machines we desperately need, and you will address him with the respect he deserves." Eviscerus merely stared at the necrotech, unfazed by Chatterbane’s disrespectful tone. Nekane was honestly uncertain of just how aware the warcaster was of what happened around him. It was as if he existed in some kind of fugue state, and only when he was digging some ancient bit of mechanika out of the ground or some forlorn tomb did he seem wholly part of this world.

name: Name
body: "My apologies, Discerptor," Chatterbane said. "Chatterbane," Eviscerus replied in that odd lecturing voice. "Master necrotech. Modification and improvements include additional appendages, spiker, eviscerator blade, and a dual-piston reciprocating necrotite furnace." The warcaster scuttled closer to Chatterbane, hunkering down so their bony visages were face to face. "Operational status: borderline." "Borderline?" Chatterbane snarled. "How dare—" Nekane suppressed a grin. Maybe Eviscerus was more aware than she thought. "Enough. I need a status report. Now." Chatterbane shook his head, and with obvious effort, drew his attention away from Eviscerus. "Well, as I said, the deplorable state of these new ’jacks and thralls has occupied much of my time and left me with fewer hours than I would like to work on larger projects." The necrotech nodded toward the half-finished bulk of the hellraker. "If Eviscerus were to aid you, would it accelerate your timeline?" Nekane asked. Chatterbane glared at Eviscerus, who had wandered off in the direction of the hellraker. The warcaster stood in the shadow of the great machine, poking and prodding at its skeletal bulk and whispering what could be a dire incantation or, as Nekane had recently heard him recite, the entire recipe for a dish called Skell Skate Surprise.

name: Name
body: "If he can be relied upon," Chatterbane said, "then, yes, his experience and skill would cut my worktime in half. If." Nekane nodded. That was good, but she was still vulnerable, and without the hellraker, she figured her chances at defeating the Cygnarans and securing the site for the eventual Necropolis and the Well of Annihilation at about even odds. "I have one other thing for you, Wraithbinder." A strange glint appeared in Chatterbane’s optical sensors. He sounded, for lack of a better word, excited. "Follow me." Chatterbane led Nekane deeper into the helljack bay to an open space with modified ’jack hoists from which two Slayers and one other helljack hung, ready for fueling or repair. As Nekane approached the third warjack, and both the light from her armor and Chatterbane’s furnace illuminated the machine, her breath caught in her throat. "How?" Chatterbane’s grin widened. "I am partially behind schedule because I couldn’t just leave Hades in the hands of those abominable Morrowans. Such a waste. Such an affront."

name: Name
body:
Nekane reached out and placed her hand on Hades’ black hull. She’d thought him destroyed; the damage the helljack had suffered in their desperate flight from the Cygnarans had seemed too severe to even hope he might be salvaged.
"I had to use the parts from two operational Slayers to repair him, but I thought the sacrifice well worth it," Chatterbane said. "I hope you agree."
Nekane felt a surprising, almost alien surge of enormous gratitude, so strong it left her speechless for a few moments. She suppressed it. And when she found her voice, she simply said,  "You have done . . . exceedingly well, Chatterbane."
"Shall I power him up?" the necrotech asked.
Nekane nodded, nearly shaking with eagerness to be reunited with the powerful helljack.
Chatterbane performed the necessary steps to bring Hades’ cortex online, and the soft glow of the helljack’s furnace bathed Nekane in welcome Cryxlight. Hades’ presence bloomed in her mind, a mote of pure power that drove away the doubt and fear that had plagued her for weeks. She felt whole again, and her enemies would suffer for that recovery.

name: Name
body:
Duke Sunbright had returned from Whiterock Fortress with more troops than he’d left with. That brought Swift Sergeant Dana Thorne some relief, though she couldn’t help but notice the duke had obviously called in his levies. Camped around the mouth of the dwarven mine were the forty or so Sunbright Yeomen the duke had taken with him when he’d returned to Whiterock, but there were another fifty men and women in mismatched kit, armed with a motley collection of rifles, pistols, and even crossbows. These were the commoners who lived in the small villages around the fortress. Useful in a pinch, but none had likely seen battle, and certainly not against a foe as terrifying as Cryx.
Dana walked toward the duke’s pavilion, sterling white flags displaying his coat of arms and the sigil of Morrow flapping in the breeze above the grand tent. She noted the slight disarray of the camp around the pavilion—the pinched faces of men and women who feared but had no real concept of the horrors they would soon face. Still, she had what she hoped was good news, and, in turn, she hoped the duke might relay some welcome news of his own.

name: Name
body:
Dana nodded at the pair of guards outside the duke’s pavilion and then ducked inside. The duke was a true fighting man and not simply an up-jumped nobleman playing at warfare. She’d seen as much in their skirmishes with the Cryxians. As such, the inside of his tent was not lavishly appointed and was, in fact, more spartan than her own accommodations with simple utilitarian furniture and racks for armor and weapons. Duke Morgan Sunbright was seated at a low table, clad in his gambeson, sharpening the spikes of his formidable morning star. He looked up as she entered.
"Swift Sergeant Thorne," he said. "Have you run our quarry to ground?"
"I have good news on that score, Your Grace," Dana said. "This Wraithbinder Nekane is crafty, and she has somehow evaded our rangers for weeks, but after she retrieved the wreck of her helljack, I knew she would eventually reveal herself."
"Your patience is to be commended. Where is our Cryxian interloper?"
"There is a strange place in the forest, not far from here, a large clearing where the ground has been burned or despoiled. We found tracks there but nowhere else."

name: Name
body:
The duke frowned and set aside his weapon. He stood and pointed at a map spread across the table before him. "Show me."
Dana tapped the spot where she and her rangers had found what appeared to be human tracks—likely thralls— and the clawed, raptor-like prints of bone or helljacks.
"I feared as much," the duke said. "That is an evil place. The site of an ancient and terrible blasphemy against the Morrowan faith during the Orgoth Occupation."
Dana shuddered. It made sense. She’d felt a queer sense of dread when she’d been there. It was too quiet, the air somehow too thick, like breathing it required a force of will. "It must be her reason for coming this far inland."
Duke Sunbright nodded. "That stands to reason. Evil attracts evil."
"Your Grace, I have rangers watching the site day and night, but I suggest we position a large force that can react quickly if Nekane returns."
"Agreed," Duke Sunbright said. "I will lead that force."
"Excellent," Dana said. "Will reinforcements from Fharin or Ironhead be joining us soon?"

name: Name
body:
The duke looked up at her, his eyes narrowing, as if in irritation. It was an odd look on his noble face. "There will be no reinforcements."
Dana blinked in surprise. "I . . . Your Grace . . . I don’t understand."
"The Sunbright Yeoman and my levies, along with what remains of your own unit, will bring this Cryxian threat to heel," Duke Sunbright said. "We need nothing else."
Dana could hardly believe what she was hearing. It was absurd. "Your Grace, the tracks I saw indicate Nekane has acquired more thralls and warjacks. The fact that we have seen tracks in one location and nowhere else leads me to believe she may be moving underground—these mountains are riddled with tunnels—and if that is the case, we have no way of knowing how large or powerful a force we may face. We should bolster our ranks. Now."
The duke stared at her, his blue eyes cold, his lips set in a hard line. He balled his hands into fists. "The honor of my house, my family name, is at stake. Too long has Sunbright been synonymous with failure and decline. No more. I will remove this blight from my lands myself."

name: Name
body: "This is . . . foolish," Dana said, though the word that had sprung to mind was asinine. "We have what—three functional warjacks? Peasant levies? You can’t hope to—" "If you have nothing further to report, Swift Sergeant," Duke Sunbright said, his voice rising. Dana stood for a moment, stunned, furious, and utterly helpless. Then she clenched her teeth and bowed. "Nothing further, Your Grace." "Then Morrow’s blessings be upon you, Sergeant."

name: Name
body:
Nekane stood at the mouth of a wide tunnel, one of the many labyrinthine passageways Eviscerus had dug beneath the mountains over the centuries. Moonlight splashed into the gloom and reflected off the iron hulls of Nekane’s helljacks and the blades and spikes of two dozen mechanithralls behind them. The tunnel reeked of necrotite, and Nekane breathed deeply, letting the burning fumes sear her throat and lungs. It was a baptism in death, one that made her feel more connected to the necromechanikal machines she would soon command in battle.
The moon-washed glow from above was suddenly obscured by three figures: the Furies returning from their scouting mission. The wraiths glided toward Nekane.
"How many?" she asked. She knew the Cygnarans waited above, their forces spread out in the trees surrounding the blasted heath that marked the site of the Vicarate Slaughter, but their numbers had grown since last she’d battled them.
"Many souls," Dogreth hissed.
"Machines of steel and fire," added Valak.

name: Name
body:
"The bright one leads," finished Anathan, a note of disgust in her whispering tones. The presence of Duke Sunbright and his strong Morrowan faith would be a thorn in the side of ancient wraiths.
Getting a straight answer out of the Furies was never easy. Their minds were half in and half out of the material world, and something so real and solid as counting enemy troops was nearly beyond them. Controlling her annoyance, Nekane repeated herself. "How many?"
The Furies stood silently, and finally Anathan spoke, his voice distant and strained, almost pained.
"One hundred," he said, the answer carrying an almost questioning tone. "Three warjacks."
Nekane nodded, appreciating how the wraith must have had to plumb the depths of memories so distant they might as well be dreams to secure the information he needed. The Cygnarans were clearly waiting for her, as she’d hoped. She’d been utilizing the underground network of tunnels to move since she’d nearly been killed by Duke Sunbright and his rangers, but she’d recently brought a small force of thralls and helljacks to the surface, here, and paraded them about, leaving obvious clues for anyone who bothered to look. The Cygnarans had looked, and they meant to ambush her here. She would turn that stratagem around and counter-ambush, wresting the element of surprise from her foes and wielding it against them.

name: Name
body:
The Cygnarans had the numbers, but Nekane’s troops were of superior quality and durability. She also had more helljacks and bonejacks than her enemy had warjacks. All this amounted to a slight advantage . . . if she executed her battle plan flawlessly.
Half of her available forces awaited her command behind her. The other half were positioned in yet another tunnel two miles away and led by Eviscerus, who was in turn supervised by Chatterbane. Once Nekane had joined the battle and drawn the Cygnaran forces out into the open, Eviscerus would lead his thralls and helljacks into the conflict, pinning the enemy between them and ultimately annihilating them.
It was a solid, workable plan but one that relied on two galling variables. First, she needed Duke Sunbright to commit his entire force to the fight, and then she needed Eviscerus’ mind to remain stable long enough so he could execute his part of her strategy. She didn’t like it, but this was the best opportunity she had to destroy her enemies and gain complete control of the site she’d traveled across oceans and mountains to secure.

name: Name
body:
Another deep breath, another searing jolt of death, and Nekane charged toward the surface.
***
Gunfire erupted from the woods—bullets shrieked by or slammed into Nekane’s power field in tiny blossoms of green light. The shredding report of storm throwers from a pair of Courser light warjacks punctuated the staccato fusillade.
Nekane commanded Hades, one of the ancient Slayers, and a Deathripper bonejack. She stood in the center of the great clearing of the Vicarate Slaughter, urging Hades to fire his soul cannon into the trees where the Cygnarans had, thus far, refused to leave cover. Bursts of necrotic energy blasted apart tall pines and spruces, occasionally obliterating Cygnaran rangers hiding behind them.
She ordered the Slayer into a charge, aiming the helljack at a plume of black smoke some fifty yards away, the coal boom from the Ironclad that Hades had nearly destroyed in their last encounter. Controlling the Slayer was more difficult than she’d anticipated. The unfamiliar helljack’s cortex was a raging storm of animalistic savagery that vaguely reminded her of the Orgoth warjacks she’d seen among Sabbreth’s forces.

name: Name
body:
The Furies, largely immune to the Cygnarans’ weapons, flitted between the trees, ripping apart the enemy with shadowy talons or destroying them utterly with bursts of razored darkness.
Nekane held her mechanithralls back—they surrounded her and Hades in a wall of undead flesh. They were taking the brunt of the enemy fire, but she wasn’t ready to commit them to the battle yet. Not until the Cygnarans believed their victory assured. Not until the Duke Sunbright left the cover of the trees to claim his glory.
The Slayer had found and engaged the Ironclad, and Nekane viewed the initial conflict through the helljack’s eyes. The Ironclad still bore the scars from its battle with Hades, and it was missing huge sections of armor, but it appeared fully functional otherwise. Nekane pushed the Slayer into a charge, and it crashed into the Cygnaran warjack, both deathclaws shredding more of the Ironclad’s hull. The warjack staggered back but swung its quake hammer in retreat, striking the Slayer a solid blow that sent it reeling.

name: Name
body:
Nekane pulled away from the Slayer, leaving it to fight on its own, and focused her attention on the Deathripper positioned on the edge of the trees. She channeled a spell through the bonejack’s arc node, shielding her mechanithralls with blurring magic to confound the Cygnaran rifles and keep her thralls upright a little longer.
The first specters of doubt began to swirl through Nekane’s mind as the Cygnarans kept firing from cover, but the gunshots finally faded to a trickle and stopped. A hoarse cry echoed from the darkened forest, a single voice that brought a grim smile to Nekane’s lips.
"For Morrow! For Cygnar!"
Duke Sunbright, his white armor glaring through the darkness, charged through the trees, his Courser warjacks pounding along beside him. Dozens of Cygnaran rangers followed in his holy wake, rifles slung, long knives gleaming like steel fangs in the moonlight.
One of the Furies—Dogreth it looked like—flitted from the shadows beneath a towering spruce and swept toward the Morrowan. Nekane could do nothing to stop what she knew was about to happen. As Dogreth closed in, spectral talons reaching, Duke Sunbright swung his morning star. The blessed weapon smashed into the Fury, and the woods echoed with the wraith’s pained howl. The Morrowan’s advance was unchecked, and Dogreth disappeared, though Nekane could not say for certain if the wraith had been destroyed or had simply retreated into the earth.

name: Name
body:
The Cygnarans stormed into the clearing and crashed into the first line of mechanithralls. The sturdy wall of undead flesh checked their advance, but it wouldn’t hold. Nekane sent Hades into the fray, targeting one of the Courser warjacks, while she aimed her rune caster at the other, firing arcane-infused bolts in a withering burst.
The battle became a brutal grind, a swirling melee between the living and the dead, where neither seemed to have the advantage. The rangers were more numerous, but their mechanithrall opponents were tougher, hit harder, and for every thrall that was destroyed, two rangers were slain.
A staggering jolt of phantom pain struck Nekane. She switched her focus to the Slayer she’d sent to occupy the Ironclad. The Cygnaran machine had landed a decisive blow with its quake hammer, and the Slayer was on its back. Nekane had a brief glimpse of the Ironclad lifting its weapon, and then the Slayer disappeared from her mind. Seconds later, the Cygnaran warjack, half-wrecked but still operational, burst from the trees and hammered into Nekane’s dwindling force of mechanithralls. Three of the undead warriors were smashed into pulp, and Nekane was forced to pull Hades away from the Courser it was battling to keep the Ironclad from wrecking what remained of her line.

name: Name
body:
Duke Sunbright, his blessed morning star casting a blinding white radiance, was fighting his way through the mechanithralls, his target obvious. Nekane considered letting him come through to challenge her directly—but not yet. She urged her Deathripper, still lingering near the trees, into a run, aiming it at the Cygnaran knight. It loped into view and threw itself into the rangers surrounding Sunbright. The duke had no choice but to turn and face this new threat, but he was unfazed. Nekane felt the brutal caress of his morning star on the Deathripper as he caved in its hull and crushed one of its legs.
More mechanithralls fell around Nekane, and the Cygnarans encircled what was left of her meager forces. She’d killed dozens, but it mattered little; enough remained to overwhelm her. She’d coaxed Duke Sunbright into the open, engaged his forces in open battle, but the other part of her plan had not materialized. Eviscerus should have arrived by now, should have come thundering in behind the Cygnarans, a hammer to crush them against the anvil of she and Hades.

name: Name
body: Was she betrayed? Had Eviscerus divined some advantage in letting her be destroyed? It mattered little now. She pushed these thoughts aside, and fought on, scything through the melee toward Duke Sunbright. She would tear his soul from his body and see it consumed before death claimed her.

name: Name
body:
Swift Sergeant Dana Thorne rammed her knife into the skull of a mechanithrall, twisted the weapon, and then kicked the half-undead, half-machine abomination away. She stood, panting, her right arm numb, blood running down her face from a shallow wound on her scalp. In the brief respite, the impossible dawned on her. They were winning.
The Cryxians had appeared in the blighted clearing just as they’d hoped, and Duke Sunbright had led the attack on the warcaster and what looked to be a smallish force of mechanithralls and helljacks. Dana smelled a trap, but the duke would not be deterred. She’d at least convinced him to attack at range first, and the rifles of his rangers and conscripted soldiers had reduced the Cryxian numbers considerably.
Then, eager to claim glory and divine retribution, Duke Sunbright charged. She’d thought it foolish. She’d thought it too soon, but here they were, surrounding the Cryxians, the enemy numbers dwindling rapidly, their own holding firm.
Dana watched Duke Sunbright’s morning star descend, a blazing nimbus of pure light, and strike Nekane, causing her to stumble back, wounded. Soon it would end. Soon Gendry and all the others destroyed and consumed by their hateful foe would be avenged.

name: Name
body: She pushed aside pain, pushed aside gnawing fatigue, and charged into the melee, her heart soaring with the glorious prospect of victory.

name: Name
body:
Nekane’s power field flared as Duke Sunbright’s morning star smashed into it like a descending meteor. The weapon crashed through, and Nekane threw herself to the side to avoid a skull-crushing blow. She took a glancing strike to the side of her head and staggered backward, teeth clenched in pain.
The duke pressed his advantage, swinging his weapon with almost reckless force. Nekane gave ground, trying to find an opening around the Duke’s shield with her hellspike, but her thrusts were deflected harmlessly by his blessed steel.
She shoved mechanithralls into the duke’s path and desperately reached out to Hades. The helljack was pinned in by the Ironclad and the remaining Courser and could not come to her aid. The damage to Hades was mounting, and a sharp pain in her head and the phantom aches along her limbs told her he would soon fall.
She evaded another strike from the duke’s morning star, and the miss left him vulnerable for a heartbeat. When his shield dipped, Nekane lashed out with her hellspike, slashing the duke’s face as he tried to jerk back out of range. The wound was hardly mortal, but seeing the duke’s blood flow brought a smile to Nekane’s face.

name: Name
body: The duke wiped blood from his wound, smearing the back of his pristine white gauntlet with crimson, and pointed his weapon at Nekane. "Sunbright Yeoman," he called out, "bring her down." Nekane saw an unwinnable battle before her. Without Eviscerus’ forces, there was simply no hope of victory. Escape was her only choice, and she prepared to shield herself in protective magic before a desperate flight. Still, she hesitated. Part of her would rather die than fail again, and as she wrestled with that awful decision, a distant tremor shook the ground beneath her feet. The tremor grew in strength. Then, it was joined by a mechanical whirring noise, steel clashing against steel in an endless cacophonous loop. The enemy felt and heard the disturbance as well, and they hesitated, drawing back from the melee. Nekane grinned wolfishly. She knew what that sound meant. She knew what was approaching. All she need do now was direct it to where it would do the most damage. She charged into the enemy, avoiding Duke Sunbright for the moment, and cut down rangers with scything blows from her hellspike. Each death filled her body with ghostly power, and as she became wraith-like, she did not use her incorporeality to flee. Instead, she used it to drive deep into the Cygnarans until she was completely surrounded and the power of her magic and the necrotite furnace on her back acted like a deathly beacon, drawing destruction up from below.

name: Name
body:
Before the Cygnarans realized what was happening, the ground bulged beneath them, and a great mound of scorched soil rose into the air, flinging aside the enemy like ants tumbling off a mound. Nekane leapt away as the bulge reached its apex and the earth split asunder to disgorge a towering horror.
The hellraker exploded from the tunnel it had carved, a great steel worm crowned with a head of razored mandibles, whirling iron drills, and glowing green eyes. A pair of segmented limbs, each ending in a massive, scythe-like blade, waved in the air, and the stench of necrotite bloomed over the battlefield as the colossal reared up, its head thirty feet above the ground.
Cries of alarm and terror rose up from the Cygnarans, but these were drowned out by the deafening mechanical whirring emanated from the hellraker’s body. It leveled its insectoid head at the enemies below it and spewed razor shrapnel across the battlefield in a series of shredding bursts. Cygnarans were torn to pieces, their corpses reduced to so much mangled meat in seconds.

name: Name
body:
The sight of the hellraker drove new strength into Nekane’s limbs, but what she saw next banished all thoughts of death and failure and filled her instead with heady joy. Discerptor Eviscerus climbed out of the hellraker’s tunnel followed by a swarm of mechanithralls. The thralls fell upon the enemy, who were still reeling from the appearance of the hellraker. A grand slaughter commenced.
Nekane cast about until she found Duke Sunbright in the chaos. The Morrowan, his white armor dulled beneath a film of dirt and blood, stood alone and unguarded, staring in dumb horror as his troops were massacred around him. His back was to Nekane, and she aimed the grappling hook mounted in the gauntlet next to her hellspike at him and fired. The jagged tines pierced the duke’s backplate and penetrated deep. With her target ensnared, Nekane pulled savagely on the wire connecting her hook to the duke’s body and yanked him backward off his feet. He crashed to the ground, and Nekane leapt upon him, ramming her knee into the center of his back, pinning him to the dirt.

name: Name
body:
As the duke struggled to rise, Nekane tore his helmet off, grabbed a hank of his hair, and jerked his head back, exposing his neck. She extended her hellspike to its fell length and placed the blade against the duke’s throat.
"Before you die, know this, Morrowan," Nekane whispered. "All you cherish, all you love, will be reduced to ash. Your god will die, your faith will become extinct, and your name will be nothing more than a footnote in a history no one will remember."
Duke Sunbright opened his mouth to say something, perhaps a plea for mercy, perhaps a prayer to his god, but Nekane drew her blade across his throat, turning his final words into a bubbling gasp. She held him down as he bled out, reveling in his twitching death throes, and when he was gone, she welcomed victory.

name: Name
body: Nekane found Chatterbane hovering over the wreckage of the Deathripper bonejack and what was left of the Cygnaran warjacks. He was already beginning to dismantle the machines for parts. Behind the necrotech, the great looming form of the hellraker lay inert, its huge furnace cooling. There had been just enough necrotite to power its short journey to the surface and its brief but devastating attack on the enemy. "My apologies, Wraithbinder," Chatterbane said when he saw Nekane approaching. "I urged Discerptor Eviscerus to lead the attack as planned, but he had . . . other ideas." Nekane shook her head. "We are victorious. That is enough, but tell me how. The hellraker was weeks from being operational." "For all his peculiarities, Lord Eviscerus has an understanding of necromechanika that is beyond even my vast skills," Chatterbane conceded. "The hellraker should not have functioned in its current state, could not have. . . yet here it is." Nekane glanced over at Eviscerus where he stood next to the colossal, his spidery limbs playing over an unfinished section of the machine while he muttered and whispered to himself. Nekane approached and cleared her throat to get the warcaster’s attention. "My thanks, Discerptor. You have helped secure a great victory for the Necrofactorium. Dominarch Deneghra will be pleased."

name: Name
body:
Eviscerus turned and regarded Nekane, the blank skull of his face unreadable. He said nothing for a moment, and then, "Wraithbinder Nekane, Iosan, protégé of the eldritch Ghyrrshyld." He paused then drew close. "Capable, ruthless, skilled. Much potential."
Nekane felt a surge of pride that the ancient warcaster had at last acknowledged her, even if it were in his own incredibly strange fashion. "Can I count on your continued support then? You will aid me in the construction of the Necropolis."
"Necropolis . . . " Eviscerus whispered, and Nekane sensed that one of those rare moments of lucidity might manifest. "I will build the Necropolis as Dominarch Deneghra commanded."
It was the longest and clearest statement Nekane had heard from the warcaster, and it filled her with equal parts dread and excitement. "What are you saying? Has the dominarch been in contact with you? Did she set you in my path?"
Eviscerus favored Nekane with another of his inscrutable expressions and did not reply but instead simply drifted off, leaving her to wonder at the depths of Deneghra’s machinations. How foolish she’d been to believe the dominarch would entrust the success of this mission to her alone. Of course Deneghra had had fail-safes in place. Eviscerus was one of them. There were bound to be others.

name: Name
body:
With difficulty, Nekane pushed her doubts aside. There was too much to do to dwell on what was beyond her control. She had still been victorious; she had still accomplished her mission. She drew in a deep breath and surveyed the eventual site of the Necropolis. Over a hundred corpses were scattered across the blighted clearing, and the pain and despair of their deaths would enhance the power of the place. Some of the corpses would be turned into thralls while those too badly mangled would provide organic components for other projects, of which there would be many.
Nekane caught sudden movement out of the corner of her eye, and saw a lone Cygnaran ranger at the edge of the battlefield, badly wounded, attempting to crawl into the tree line. She smiled, extended her hellspike, and went to make her triumph complete.
***
Swift Sergeant Dana Thorne crawled toward the forest, her shattered leg sending waves of agony through her body with every move. The pain was nothing compared to the horror she’d just witnessed. There were no words for it. Part of her simply wanted to lie down and die simply so she wouldn’t have to think about the abomination that had come crawling out of the earth.

name: Name
body:
But she was a survivor, and so she crawled, slowly, hoping to evade detection from the thralls and the other blighted terrors dragging away the corpses of her companions to work further blasphemies on their flesh.
She’d almost made it to the trees when she felt sudden, terrible pressure in the middle of her back that crushed the air from her lungs. She gasped and tried to draw her long knife, but the pressure increased, and she could do little but squirm helplessly beneath it.
"What have we here? A survivor?" a rasping, feminine voice said, and Dana squeezed her eyes shut in terror. The pressure disappeared, and Wraithbinder Nekane kicked Dana onto her back with an armored foot.
Now Dana did manage to draw her knife, and she slashed at the Cryxian warcaster above her. Nekane stepped out of range and laughed.
"Such spirit," she said and leveled the bladed gauntlet on her right arm at Dana.
Dana tried to rise to her feet, broken leg be damned, and she made it her knees before Nekane fired her weapon. The breath left Dana’s lungs in an agonizing rush and her mouth filled with blood. She looked down at a fist-sized hole in her chest and collapsed onto her back again, her final breaths oozing between her lips in a liquid wheeze.

name: Name
body:
Nekane leaned over Dana, the horrid stench of necrotite—rotting flesh and voided bowels—filling her nose just as the terror of impending death filled her mind. The Cryxian warcaster smiled.
"Yes, such spirit," she said with a vile grin. "You’ll make an exemplary thrall."

name: Waking the Dead\nPart 4 - Chapter 1 Waking the Dead: Part 4
